Description: Cross-platform PowerShell 7 CLI that consolidates the authoring and CI tooling for Azure Verified Modules (https://aka.ms/avm). A single avm command (alias: avm) works across both ecosystems and ships: environment diagnostics (avm version, avm doctor); a checksum-pinned managed-tool resolver (avm tool list/which/install) that downloads and verifies the exact terraform, terraform-docs, tflint, conftest and mapotf binaries a module needs; and a fully wired Terraform authoring chain - avm pre-commit fixes and checks a module locally (convention checks, HCL transforms via mapotf, terraform fmt and terraform-docs) while avm pr-check adds tflint, APRL/AVMSEC policy checks and terraform validate. No Docker, make or porch required. The Bicep facade is in active development. Requires PowerShell 7.4+ (Core). See https://github.com/Azure/azure-verified-modules-tools for status and docs.

Manage Entra ID and Azure RBAC building blocks across tenants: Entra ID groups, PIM, Administrative Units, Entitlement Management, Access Reviews, Azure resources and RBAC, plus a JSON inventory and declarative apply engine.

Manage a PagerArchive server from PowerShell: sign in with your PagerArchive account, manage templates and aliases, import aliases through the pipeline, search and watch messages, and back up the server now.

This script creates everything CertKit needs to deploy certificates to Microsoft Entra Application Proxy applications using client secret authentication, following least privilege.

- A dedicated app registration and service principal for CertKit.
- A custom Entra role that can only read Application Proxy settings and update the Application Proxy SSL certificate.
- The read-only Microsoft Graph application permission Application.Read.All, used by CertKit to find App Proxy applications.
- A tenant-wide assignment of the custom role to the CertKit service principal, made directly or through Privileged Identity Management (PIM).
- A client secret, which is copied to the clipboard and never displayed on screen.

The script is safe to run more than once. Existing objects with the same names are reused, and existing role and permission assignments are not duplicated. A new client secret is created on every run. Use -RemoveExistingSecrets to remove older client secrets after the new one is created.
